channel.title: Behavioural Science Daily Brief
channel.description: A daily reading of new working papers, peer-reviewed articles and policy work in behavioural science, psychology and behavioural economics, prepared for a first-year undergraduate on the LSE BSc Psychological and Behavioural Science. Each episode gives the finding, the method, the sample and the limitations, with a concept of the day and a note on research methods.

item.title: Saturday 7 November 2026
item.description: A British school-leaving law and dementia fifty years on, voters who prefer an improving trend to a better one, magnetic stimulation of the brain's meaning network, a perceptual marker for social anxiety that three experiments could not find, a meditation trial beaten by muscle relaxation, and punishment in two very different societies. The concept of the day is what a stimulation study establishes that an imaging study cannot, and the methods watch is an indexing decision that quietly reshapes the evidence base.

item.title: Friday 6 November 2026
item.description: A new scale claims East Asia is far more collectivist than the old questionnaires could see; brain volumes predict impatience without describing the impatience task; gracious defeat in sport transfers to political judgement; isolation and loneliness buy four months of biological age; schizophrenia and reading anger from points of light; and machine medical advice in Mumbai. The concept of the day is the discount rate, and why the task makes the number.

item.title: Thursday 5 November 2026
item.description: A Nigerian television drama that moved beliefs about reporting corruption by fifty points and reporting itself not at all; reappraisal in the autistic brain; blink rates and rule-switching in preschoolers; self-rated masculinity and political attitudes; reward and memory; dark traits and poor reasoning. The concept of the day is the third variable that moves both of your measures, and the methods watch is differential exclusion.

item.title: Wednesday 4 November 2026
item.description: Six items: a reflection on the surface of the eye that turns out to be a gaze cue, childbirth trauma measured the same way in thirty-one countries, liberals and dominant leaders, people misjudging their opponents' open-mindedness, an audit of AI search summaries, and wildfire smoke in pregnancy. The concept of the day is what makes something a perceptual cue and how you show one is used.
